'''''Euphorbia umbellata''''', the '''African milkbush''', is a species in the [[spurge family]] from Africa.

==Description==
African milkbushes are moderate sized shrubs to medium trees growing {{Convert|2–10|m|ft|round=0.5|sp=us}} tall.<ref name="Beentje 1994">{{cite book |last1=Beentje |first1=Henk |title=Kenya Trees, Shrubs, and Lianas |date=1994 |publisher=National Museums of Kenya |location=Nairobi, Kenya |isbn=978-9966-9861-0-8 |page=224 |url=https://archive.org/details/kenyatreesshrubs0000been |access-date=16 July 2026}}</ref> The young stems have a fleshy texture.<ref name="Eggli & Nyffeler 2023" /> The leaves are attached directly to stems by their base and either have smooth edges or very small teeth towards the ends.<ref name="Eggli & Nyffeler 2023" /> Wild specimens have green leaves that are sometimes somewhat red colored on the undersides,<ref name="Eggli & Nyffeler 2023" /> however garden plants with fully or partly purplish red leaves are in cultivation.<ref name="Smith & Van Wyk 2008" /> They measure {{Cvt|6–15|cm|round=0.5}} long by {{Cvt|2–6|cm|round=0.5}} wide.<ref name="Beentje 1994" />

==Taxonomy==
In 1894 [[Ferdinand Albin Pax]] described a species which he named ''Synadenium umbellatum''.<ref name="POWO" /> In 2006 research into the DNA of ''Synadenium'' indicated that it should be merged with the ''[[Euphorbia]]'' genus.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bruyns |first1=Peter V. |last2=Mapaya |first2=Ruvimbo J. |last3=Hedderson |first3=Terrence J. |title=A new subgeneric classification for ''Euphorbia'' (Euphorbiaceae) in southern Africa based on ITS and psbA-trnH sequence data |journal=Taxon |date=May 2006 |volume=55 |issue=2 |pages=397–420 |doi=10.2307/25065587 |jstor=25065587 |bibcode=2006Taxon..55..397B |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233675476 |access-date=15 July 2026}}</ref> The new name for the species, ''Euphorbia umbellata'', was published by Peter Vincent Bruyns in 2007. Together with its genus it is classified in the [[Euphorbiaceae]] family. Including its previous name it has four [[botanical synonym]]s.<ref name="POWO" /> Prior to its reclassification ''Synadenium grantii'' was typically used for the species, including in scientific texts,<ref name="Beentje 1994" /> but this name should not be confused with ''[[Euphorbia grantii]]''.<ref>{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |date=2026 |id=346682-1 |title=''Euphorbia grantii'' Oliv. |access-date=16 July 2026}}</ref>

''Euphorbia umbellata'' is known by the [[common name]]s ''African milk bush'',<ref name="Smith & Van Wyk 2008">{{cite book |last1=Smith |first1=Gideon |last2=Van Wyk |first2=Ben-Erik |title=The Garden Succulents Primer |date=2008 |publisher=Timber Press |location=Portland, Oregon |isbn=978-0-88192-954-6 |page=180 |url=https://archive.org/details/gardensucculents0000smit |access-date=16 July 2026}}</ref> ''African milk-bush'',<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Quattrocchi |first1=Umberto |date=2012 |title=CRC World Dictionary of Medicinal and Poisonous Plants |location=Boca Raton, Florida |publisher=CRC Press |page=1700 |isbn=978-1-4822-5064-0 |oclc=874163087}}</ref> and ''African milkbush'', due to the poisonous, white latex sap produced from wounds.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hecht |first1=Hans |title=Cacti & Succulents |date=1994 |publisher=Sterling Pub. Co |location=New York |isbn=978-0-8069-0548-8 |page=120 |url=https://archive.org/details/cactisucculents0000hech_k7p8 |access-date=16 July 2026}}</ref>

==Range==
''Euphorbia umbellata'' is native to eastern areas in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Tanzania along both shores of [[Lake Tanganyika]] as well as in western Kenya and Uganda.<ref name="Eggli & Nyffeler 2023">{{Cite book |last1=Eggli |first1=Urs |last2=Nyffeler |first2=Reto |date=2023 |title=Dicotyledons: Rosids |edition=Second |location=Cham, Germany |publisher=Springer |pages=589–590 |doi=10.5962/bhl.title.48631 |isbn=978-3-030-93491-0 |oclc=5036602}}</ref> According to [[Plants of the World Online]] it is also native in Rwanda and South Sudan, but is doubtfully present in Malawi.<ref name="POWO" /> It is found at elevations of {{Convert|950|to(-)|2100|m|sp=us}} on rocky slopes in open woodlands.<ref name="Eggli & Nyffeler 2023" />

It grows as an introduced plant in Bangladesh and India.<ref name="POWO" />

==Uses==
African milkbush is cultivated in tropical gardens as well as a container plant. Plants are typically grown from cuttings and are regarded as easy to cultivate in gardens. The [[cultivar]] 'Rubra' with solid purple-red leaves is valued by gardeners for adding year round color to landscapes.<ref name="Smith & Van Wyk 2008" />
